messages:
Maria G: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can leadership expand on the 'how we win' thesis a bit? When we say 'serving beats model ownership' what are the practical priorities for teams: do we push customers to `Hosted` for PLG motion, promote `Dedicated` for predictability, or invest more in `Private` for enterprise deals? Also curious how partnerships (model providers/cloud partners) fit vs building more differentiated product features.

Celine (CEO): Short version: product teams should prioritize where it reduces customer friction and aligns with SLAs. For growth we default to `Hosted` -> fastest onboarding. For predictable revenue and SLOs push `Dedicated`. For regulated customers or strategic infra deals, `Private`. Partnerships are complementary — we don't treat them as a substitute for product differentiation.

Devon (Eng): To add: technical constraints matter. If a workload needs strict latency & KV cache locality, `Dedicated` or `Private` wins. We're rolling out better batching heuristics to make `Hosted` handle more bursty apps without blowing up cost.

Anya (Product): From a GTM POV, frame it as tiers: PLG users start on `Hosted` with easy migrations to `Dedicated` once they hit commit thresholds. `Private` is sales-led. Our console/rollout features should make that migration >90% frictionless.

Jamal (Sales): Helpful — on the field we hear two asks: (1) cheaper per-token for high-volume NLP (recommendations/rerank) and (2) isolation for compliance. Both translate into clear upsell paths if we show cost delta + perf SLOs. Would love a simple slide we can share with prospects.

Celine (CEO): Good call, Jamal — we'll put together a one-pager with cost/latency tradeoffs and migration story. High-level bullets: Hosted = fastest time-to-value, Dedicated = predictable throughput & cost controls, Private = security/compliance + advanced KMS integrations.

Leo (Research): One nuance: our tech moat is in serving optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache, kernel selection). We should keep talking about unit economics: it's not just hosting vs private, it's 'how much infra can we save per token via runtime features'.

Devon (Eng): Also want to flag that automatic fallback policies (cheaper model variant on overload) and quantization profiles are in roadmap Q3 — that directly helps customers trade cost vs quality without manual ops.

Maria G: Awesome, thanks. Two quick follow-ups: 1) Who owns the customer-facing migration docs? 2) Any ETA on the sales one-pager?

Anya (Product): I'll own the migration docs and collaborate with DevEx. ETA for the one-pager: draft by EOW, final by next Wed. Ping me @Anya if you need early review.

ops-bot: reminder: all-hands follow-up doc uploaded -> https://internal.redwood.local/all-hands/2773334444-notes :paperclip: 

Celine (CEO): Thanks everyone. Keep feedback coming in this thread or drop concrete asks in the follow-up doc. Our north star: make inference predictable, economical, and easy to adopt — that explains every product choice. :rocket:
